analysis.title: Brace for Impact?
key_insights: Equities sold off Friday on renewed AI-trade doubts. NASDAQ closed more than 5% lower, NVIDIA fell 14% and newly listed Anthropic fell 8.5% to close a little over $5/share above its $83 list price. The VIX hit its highest reading since April 2025.

Authorities in China, South Korea and Taiwan intervened with reduced margining requirements, short-selling limits and new market stabilization funds. US equity futures point higher at the open while Asian equities are lower.
Bessent softened his stance on a shakeup at NVIDIA, saying he would not be opposed to a return of Jensen Huang.

The narrative combines worries that AI leaders cannot grow into valuations and that capex may not be justified by cashflows, with fears that resilient US activity plus war and tariff supply pressures push central banks to hike more aggressively. This hurts long-duration growth stocks.

Fed Governor Cook said skipping a rate hike in October risks putting the Fed behind the curve. She cited AI investment as an inflation driver and warned that falling behind could require steeper hikes later. Waller has also been hawkish.

Bill Ackman argues the Fed is about to make a mistake, citing higher SpaceX debt financing costs and a higher cost of equity after stock falls. He says investment needs from geopolitics have supplanted the 2% inflation target.

Market signals support the policy-error argument. The US 5y5y inflation swap fell from 2.47% to 2.32%, its lowest since March. IG CDS widened in Europe and the Americas, and the USD is at its strongest since Liberation Day last year.
OIS-implied Fed tightening out to September next year fell from 84bps to 62bps in a week. Sharp falls in gold, silver and bitcoin late last week looked like a scramble for liquidity.

Australia is a case study. The RBA hiked five times this year to 4.85%. October jobs fell 45,300 and unemployment rose from 4.7% to 4.9%, above NAIRU and close to triggering the Sahm Rule. Services PMI fell from 48.5 to 46.2.
Australia October CPI is due Wednesday with headline expected to rise from 4.3% to 4.8%. Markets fully price a 25bp RBA cut by June 2027 and a 73% probability of a second cut by Christmas 2027.

Peace hopes faded after the Trump, Xi and Putin 'Yalta 2.0' meeting at APEC produced no progress. Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy, Houthi strikes on Riyadh and Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping continue. Oil curves remain in steep backwardation, implying a war premium, though the long end of the Brent curve has fallen.

COP31 in Türkiye collapsed over fossil fuel transition language, with Saudi-led Arab League, Russia and India resisting the EU. Rabobank flags escalation risks while noting a possible future of more abundant hydrocarbons, which may arrive too late to avoid demand shocks.
Week ahead includes US October PCE on Wednesday (headline seen 3.6% to 3.8%, core 3.1% to 3.2%), Australia CPI, US Q3 GDP second read, Beige Book, and Europe, UK and US flash PMIs Monday.

tension_points.bull_case: Cook and Waller argue the Fed risks falling behind the curve, with AI investment driving inflation, so steeper hikes may be needed later.
tension_points.bear_case: Ackman argues the Fed is about to err. Falling 5y5y inflation swap, wider IG CDS, strong USD and Australia's weakening economy suggest tightening is overdone.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hot October PCE (headline 3.8%, core 3.2% expected) would favour the hawks, while a weak print would support the policy-error view.
